newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Meyer says SNB helped Swiss growth.
newsitem.headline: Meyer says SNB helped Swiss growth.

text.p: Swiss National Bank chairman Hans Meyer said the central bank had done all it could for the time being to help revive the stagnant Swiss economy.
"We believe that we have played our part in this phase," Meyer told a news conference.
Meyer also said he saw no deflationary threat for the moment.
"We are not of the opinion that the problem in the next phase lies with monetary policy," Meyer said, when asked whether the SNB could do more to boost the Swiss economy.
Meyer said monetary policy was just one influence alongside government financial policy and competition policy.
Asked whether Switzerland was facing a deflationary threat, Meyer said:
"We don't believe there is an immediate risk, but we understand that we have to keep an eye on the problem."
Asked whether the SNB would consider further cuts in its discount rate, Meyer said the SNB had done its part to help the Swiss economy.
"This implies the view that we don't think monetary policy would play the central role in the immediate future. However in the end, never say never," Meyer said.
